div.note: U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; Liebermann's text has two columns: H (Textus Roffensis f. 41v, after EGu in the same line and hand, c. 1120; perhaps a fragment of a law) and B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 86, after Wif, as in the Quadripartitus, c. 1125). K is B; H is also given here. B's heading is in red and not original; H has none. Liebermann dates Wer 944–c. 1060.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “944–c.1060; c.945 (Wormald)”, now “944–c.1060 (Liebermann); c.945 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “944–c.1060 (Liebermann); c.945 (Wormald)”, now “944–c.1060 (Liebermann, I p. 392); c.945 (Wormald, MEL pp. 374–8)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “B 392; Q 393; German 393”; 11 rows of Wer)

note.seg: Die Überschrift, laut des Fehlers und der nur teilweisen Umfassung des Inhalts sicher nicht original, ist wahrscheinlich archetyp, da sie, obwohl H fehlend und in Q abweichend, dieselbe Form zeigt wie die zu Swerian (o. I 396) und Wif (o. I 442), welche Stücke in hbq neben Wer standen

The heading, certainly not original in view of the error and of its covering the contents only in part, is probably in the archetype, since, though missing in H and different in Q, it shows the same form as those to Swerian (above I 396) and Wif (above I 442), pieces which stood alongside Wer in hbq
